`rollingUpdate` sub-fields, and Kubernetes rejects the apply because
`rollingUpdate` is forbidden when type is `Recreate`.

Fix with a JSON patch to remove the stale fields:

```bash
kubectl patch deployment <name> -n <ns> --type='json' \
  -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/strategy/rollingUpdate"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/strategy/type","value":"Recreate"}]'
```

Alternatively, force a full resource replacement:

```bash
argocd app sync <app> --replace
```

# mothership-gitops

GitOps manifests for `talos-prod-01` Kubernetes cluster.

## Repo Boundary

This repo answers: what runs on the cluster after the Omni-managed Talos
substrate exists?

mothership-gitops owns ArgoCD App of Apps reconciliation, sync waves, Longhorn
Helm values, backup schedules, StorageClasses, ESO/Infisical wiring, Tailscale
Operator manifests, ingress exposure, monitoring, dashboards, and workload
applications.

It does not own the Omni substrate. Sidero Omni self-hosting, the Proxmox
infrastructure provider, cluster templates, machine classes, Talos node
requirements, SideroLink/DNS/Tailscale access constraints, and provider
troubleshooting live in `../Omni-Scale`. This repo may reference substrate
constraints when they affect platform bootstrap, such as the required Cilium
MTU override, but Omni-Scale is the source of truth for why those constraints
exist.

## Architecture

App of Apps pattern with sync waves. Bootstrap installs prerequisites first,
then ArgoCD reconciles:

1. ArgoCD (non-HA via Helm)
2. External Secrets Operator + Infisical ClusterSecretStores
3. Tailscale Operator + Ingress for ArgoCD
4. Longhorn (distributed storage) + Ingress
5. Netdata (monitoring)
6. Radar (Kubernetes UI and MCP server)
7. Homarr (homelab dashboard)
8. Anthropic OAuth Proxy (tailnet-microservices Kustomize)
9. Phoenix (LLM observability eval backend)
10. ArgoCD HA upgrade (manual trigger)

All web UIs exposed via Tailscale Ingress (no public exposure).

## Bootstrap

The bootstrap requires pre-installing CNI, ESO, and Longhorn via Helm before
ArgoCD can manage them. This breaks a chicken-and-egg: ArgoCD needs CNI to
schedule, ESO needs CRDs before ClusterSecretStores, Longhorn hooks need the
ServiceAccount the chart creates.

### Prerequisites

- `kubectl` configured via Omni proxy
- `helm` CLI
- Infisical Universal Auth credentials (Machine Identity)

### Deploy

```bash
# 1. Create bootstrap secret for ESO
kubectl create namespace external-secrets
kubectl create secret generic universal-auth-credentials \
  --from-literal=clientId=<INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID> \
  --from-literal=clientSecret=<INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET> \
  -n external-secrets

# 2. Install Cilium CNI (required before ArgoCD can schedule)
#
# MTU=1450 is MANDATORY. Omni's siderolink WireGuard tunnel runs at MTU 1280,
# which Cilium will auto-detect and apply to every pod veth cluster-wide,
# strangling all traffic through Tailscale Ingress (~22 KB/s vs ~99 Mbps).
# Never omit --set MTU=1450. See Omni-Scale/docs/guides/CILIUM.md.
CP_IP=$(kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}')
kubectl label namespace kube-system pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
helm repo add cilium https://helm.cilium.io/
helm install cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system \
  --set ipam.mode=kubernetes \
  --set kubeProxyReplacement=true \
  --set MTU=1450 \
  --set k8sServiceHost=$CP_IP \
  --set k8sServicePort=6443 \
  --set cgroup.autoMount.enabled=false \
  --set cgroup.hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup \
  --set securityContext.privileged=true

# Wait for nodes Ready
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready nodes --all --timeout=300s

# 3. Install ESO (CRDs before app-of-apps syncs ClusterSecretStores)
helm repo add external-secrets https://charts.external-secrets.io
helm install external-secrets external-secrets/external-secrets \
  -n external-secrets --set installCRDs=true

# 4. Create privileged namespaces and install Longhorn
kubectl create namespace longhorn-system
kubectl create namespace netdata
kubectl label namespace longhorn-system pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
kubectl label namespace netdata pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
helm repo add longhorn https://charts.longhorn.io
helm install longhorn longhorn/longhorn -n longhorn-system --no-hooks

# 5. Install ArgoCD via Helm
helm repo add argo https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm
helm install argocd argo/argo-cd -n argocd --create-namespace \
  --set configs.params."server\.insecure"=true \
  --set global.networkPolicy.create=false

# 6. Bootstrap app-of-apps
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/basher83/mothership-gitops/main/bootstrap/bootstrap.yaml

# 7. Monitor sync progress
watch kubectl get applications -n argocd

# 8. After all apps healthy, trigger HA upgrade
kubectl patch application argocd-ha -n argocd --type merge \
  -p '{"operation":{"sync":{}}}'
kubectl patch application argocd-ha-helm -n argocd --type merge \
  -p '{"operation":{"sync":{}}}'
```

## Recovery

Full cluster rebuild from Git:

1. Rebuild cluster via Omni (use Omni-Scale `/omni-scale:disaster-recovery`)
2. Follow Deploy steps above
3. Wait for all apps synced

Workload data in Longhorn is lost unless backed up to S3.

## Structure

```text
bootstrap/
  bootstrap.yaml        # Entry point (ArgoCD + root app)
apps/
  root.yaml             # App of Apps orchestrator
  argocd/               # HA upgrade (wave 99, manual)
  argocd-ingress/       # Tailscale Ingress for ArgoCD (wave 4)
  external-secrets/     # ESO + ClusterSecretStores (root wave 2, child waves 1-2)
  tailscale-operator/   # Tailscale Operator (wave 4)
  longhorn/             # Storage + Ingress (wave 5)
  netdata/              # Monitoring + Ingress (wave 6)
  radar/                # Kubernetes UI + MCP + Ingress (wave 6)
  homarr/               # Dashboard + Ingress (wave 7)
  anthropic-oauth-proxy.yaml  # External-source app (wave 8)
  phoenix/              # LLM observability + Ingress (wave 9)
docs/
  adrs/                 # Architecture decisions and supersession history
  incidents/            # Historical incident reports and follow-up status
```

Radar is a deliberate single-operator exception to application-level ingress
authentication. Its UI and MCP endpoint share the `radar` Tailscale hostname
and the chart ServiceAccount: pod logs and cluster resource reads are enabled,
while Secrets, Helm writes, pod exec, port-forward, and node mutations are not.
A NetworkPolicy admits the ClusterIP only from the operator-created Radar
Ingress proxy, preventing ordinary pods from bypassing Tailscale. The selected
chart, storage, access, upgrade, and validation contract is recorded in
[`../specs/radar-in-cluster.md`](../specs/radar-in-cluster.md).

Radar's canonical Git-rendered diffs use a separate ArgoCD local account with
only `applications get`. Its dedicated token flows from Infisical `/radar`
through ESO into the Radar Deployment and is pinned to the plain-HTTP
`argocd-ha-helm-server` cluster Service. The token grants no sync or mutation
authority and does not expand the chart ServiceAccount. Account and policy
changes inherit the manual `argocd-ha` and `argocd-ha-helm` promotion gates;
the Secret-backed Radar configuration follows Radar's normal automated sync.

Tailscale exposure does not make every cluster-internal route authorized. For
the credential-backed `anthropic-oauth-proxy`, tailnet membership is the
intended main-proxy boundary, while kubeconfig and Kubernetes RBAC through
port-forwarding are the intended admin boundary. The current source manifests
do not yet enforce those boundaries against ordinary cluster pods. The
selected design, evidence classification, cross-repository ownership, and
rollout gates are recorded in
[`../specs/oauth-proxy-boundary-remediation.md`](../specs/oauth-proxy-boundary-remediation.md).
This is planned work and must not be read as a claim that the findings are
remediated.

I found no documentation for the `argocd` CLI as a tool. The repo mentions it twice inside troubleshooting fixes, but never explains how to install it, log in, or use it.

**Where `argocd` CLI appears:**

1. `docs/troubleshooting.md:92` runs `argocd app sync longhorn-helm --app-namespace argocd --revision <rev>` to clear a stale failed operation. The text after it says "If an ArgoCD API session is unavailable…" and falls back to `kubectl`, so it expects you to already be logged in.
2. `docs/troubleshooting.md:388` runs `argocd app sync <app> --replace` as an alternative fix for the SSA strategy patch problem.

**What's missing:**

- **Prerequisites:** the README lists `kubectl`, `helm` and the Infisical credentials, but not `argocd`.
- **Install:** `mise.toml` pins `helm`, `kubeconform`, `pre-commit`, `ripgrep` and `yq`, but not `argocd`. There's no version pin, so the CLI could drift away from the server version.
- **Login:** nothing says how to authenticate. The server sits behind the Tailscale Ingress `argocd` (`apps/argocd-ingress/ingress.yaml`, which points at `argocd-ha-helm-server`) and runs with `server.insecure=true`. TLS ends at the Tailscale proxy, so the CLI will likely need `--grpc-web` when going through the ingress. I haven't tested this. Nothing covers where the admin credential comes from either: initial-admin-secret, SSO, or a local account.
- **Day-to-day use:** the README bootstrap uses `kubectl patch application ... operation.sync` for the HA upgrade and `watch kubectl get applications` for monitoring. Nothing shows the `argocd` equivalents (`app list`, `app get`, `app diff`, `app sync`), which are the more natural tools for the manual `argocd-ha` / `argocd-ha-helm` gates.
- **Radar account:** `specs/radar-in-cluster.md` describes the read-only `radar` local account and its token. It notes that a direct-token method was needed, but there's no general operator CLI workflow.

# ArgoCD CLI

The `argocd` CLI is a system tool installed and upgraded through Homebrew, not
pinned in this repo's `mise.toml`. This guide covers how it reaches the
`talos-prod-01` ArgoCD instance, the failure modes seen in practice, and the
commands used for routine inspection and the manual sync gates.

## Two Access Modes

The CLI keeps its contexts in `~/.config/argocd/config`, and `argocd context`
shows which one is active. Two contexts exist for this cluster, and they reach
ArgoCD by different paths.

| Context | Mode | Path to ArgoCD |
|---------|------|----------------|
| `kubernetes` | Core (`core: true`) | Kubernetes API through kubeconfig; no ArgoCD session |
| `argocd.tailfb3ea.ts.net` | Server (`grpc-web: true`) | ArgoCD API server through the Tailscale Ingress |

Core mode bypasses the ArgoCD API server and its RBAC entirely. It acts with
whatever Kubernetes identity the kubeconfig context carries, which for the
operator contexts is cluster-admin. Server mode authenticates to ArgoCD itself
and is subject to ArgoCD accounts and `policy.csv`.

## Core Mode

Core mode reads ArgoCD's ConfigMaps and Application resources from the
namespace set on the active kubeconfig context. Neither `talos-prod-01`
context sets a namespace, so core-mode commands fail with:

```text
configmap "argocd-cm" not found
```

The fix is a dedicated kubeconfig context that reuses an existing cluster and
user entry but sets `namespace: argocd`. Do not add the namespace to
`talos-prod-operator.tailfb3ea.ts.net` itself: that context is generated by
`tailscale configure kubeconfig` (see
[ADR-002](adrs/ADR-002-enable-tailscale-api-server-proxy.md)), and
regenerating it would drop the setting. A namespace on the shared context
would also change the default for every `kubectl` command.

```bash
SRC=talos-prod-operator.tailfb3ea.ts.net
kubectl config set-context talos-prod-argocd \
  --cluster="$(kubectl config view -o jsonpath="{.contexts[?(@.name==\"$SRC\")].context.cluster}")" \
  --user="$(kubectl config view -o jsonpath="{.contexts[?(@.name==\"$SRC\")].context.user}")" \
  --namespace=argocd
```

Then point core-mode commands at it explicitly:

```bash
argocd --core --kube-context talos-prod-argocd app list
```

This was verified against the Tailscale API server proxy context. The Omni
context (`omni-talos-prod-01`) should work the same way, but it has not been
tested here.

## Server Mode

Server mode talks to `argocd-ha-helm-server` through the `argocd` Tailscale
Ingress (`apps/argocd-ingress/ingress.yaml`). The server runs with
`server.insecure: true` and TLS terminates at the Tailscale proxy, so the CLI
must use gRPC-web. The saved context already has `grpc-web: true`; pass
`--grpc-web` on a fresh login.

No SSO is configured. Authentication uses the local `admin` account, whose
initial password lives in the `argocd-initial-admin-secret` Secret. Never
commit or paste that value.

```bash
argocd login argocd.tailfb3ea.ts.net --grpc-web --username admin
argocd context argocd.tailfb3ea.ts.net
```

Sessions expire. An `Unauthenticated ... Token is expired` error means the
saved context still exists but needs `argocd relogin`.

The `radar` local account is API-key only with `applications, get`. It exists
for Radar's Git-rendered diffs and is not an operator login; see
[`../specs/radar-in-cluster.md`](../specs/radar-in-cluster.md).

## Common Commands

The examples below use server mode. In core mode, prefix each with
`--core --kube-context talos-prod-argocd`.

```bash
argocd app list
argocd app get <app>
argocd app diff <app>
argocd app sync <app>
```

`argocd app get` and `argocd app diff` are read-only and safe at any time.
Before running `argocd app sync`, check the sync policy exceptions in
[`architecture.md`](architecture.md). Never pass `--prune` to `longhorn`,
`longhorn-helm`, or `coredns-tailscale`.

The manual gates (`argocd-ha`, `argocd-ha-helm`, `anthropic-oauth-proxy`) are
promoted with `argocd app sync`. Run `argocd app diff` first and read the
result, because these gates exist precisely so a human reviews the change.
`argocd-ha` creates `argocd-ha-helm` but does not sync it, so promoting
ArgoCD HA takes two syncs:

```bash
argocd app diff argocd-ha
argocd app sync argocd-ha
argocd app diff argocd-ha-helm
argocd app sync argocd-ha-helm
```

## Version Skew

Homebrew tracks the latest `argocd` release, while the server version follows
the chart behind the manual `argocd-ha-helm` gate. The two can drift apart by a
major version. `argocd version` reports both when a server session is
available. Skew matters most in core mode, where the client reads server-side
ConfigMaps and CRDs directly.

As of 2026-11-07 the Homebrew client is v3.6.1 and the live server is v2.14.11
(chart `7.9.1`). Git pins `argo-cd` chart `10.*`, so the next `argocd-ha-helm`
promotion is a major ArgoCD v2 → v3 upgrade, not a routine sync. Review the
upstream upgrade notes before running it.

- **The core-mode fix:** a separate kubeconfig context, `talos-prod-argocd`, with `namespace: argocd`, used via `argocd --core --kube-context talos-prod-argocd ...`. **Omni context:** core mode works through `omni-talos-prod-01` as well, using a separate context with `namespace: argocd`. Its kubeconfig user logs in through the `kubectl oidc-login` plugin, so the first call took about 11 seconds, probably while it refreshed the token. **Admin password:** it has never been changed. `admin.passwordMtime` in `argocd-secret` is 2026-01-15T04:53:20Z, the same timestamp as the creation of `argocd-initial-admin-secret`. A real login worked end to end: `argocd login ... --grpc-web` as `admin` with that password, then `app list`, `version` and `account get-user-info`. I used a throwaway `--config` and deleted it afterwards, so your `~/.config/argocd/config` and the expired session in it are unchanged. The doc now says the password was never rotated and shows how to read it with `argocd admin initial-password -n argocd`.

That's a security point you should decide on. The bootstrap password is still the live admin credential, and its Secret is still in the cluster. Argo CD recommends changing it and deleting `argocd-initial-admin-secret`. I didn't touch either.

**URL fix:** `apps/argocd/ha-upgrade.yaml` now sets `global.domain: argocd.tailfb3ea.ts.net`. I checked the key in the values for both chart 7.9.1 and 10.14.0. The live `url: https://argocd.example.com` is simply the chart default for `global.domain`.
